newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 16.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Relations with Slovakia are tainted by unresolved property disputes dating back to the division of the federation -- an often-repeated theme in Slovak politics. At present, neither side looks ready to resolve the disagreements.

- Czech President Vaclav Havel and Uzbek President Islam Karimov signed a declaration in Prague Castle calling for development of collaborative work between the two countries. Also signed yesterday was an agreement concerning mutual support and protection of investments, a memorandum between the Czech Trade Ministry and Uzbek External Economics Ministry and a memorandum for mutual relations between Komercni Banka and Uzbek National Bank.
- Shareholders of Kreditni Banka Plzen approved progress toward liquidation and a liquidation plan yesterday.
- The main Czech refineries increased sales of fuel and oil by one fourth last year. Ceska Rafinerska alone sold more than three million tonnes of petrol and motor oil.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Miroslav Havel, Deputy to the Finance Minister, announced yesterday that the government budget for 1996 shows a deficit of approximately 1.7 billion crowns. This total, which makes up less than one percent of GDP, should not be considered as very substantial.

- According to officials at the Finance Ministry some tens of billions of crowns, which the government would receive from proposed tax increases in energy and construction work, will be used for social aid for the poorest groups of citizens.

PRAVO - The cabinet unexpectedly voiced the opinion on Wednesday that salaries of government officials (meaning representatives, ministers, the president, members of the Supreme Control Office, directors of the BIS intelligence service and judges) should be reduced by 10 to 15 percent.

- British beer concern Bass is hoping that significant shareholders of brewery Radegast Nosovice will agree to a share increase for Bass by the end of this year. The decision depends on Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB) with a 34 percent stake and Kapitalova Investicni Spolecnost Ceske Pojistovny (KIS CP) with 23 percent of shares.
